keyTerms.definition: A warp consists of 32 threads that execute in lockstep together.
A block groups threads on one SM that share its shared memory.

recall.question: How many threads make up a warp?
recall.answer: A warp consists of 32 threads that execute in lockstep.

recall.question: 1000 threads. Warps? Blocks of 256?
recall.answer: Warps: ceil(1000/32) = 32. Blocks of 256: ceil(1000/256) = 4.

keyTerms.definition: Divergence happens when lanes of a warp take different branches, causing the warp to execute both paths serially.
A warp contains lanes that take different branches during divergence and executes both paths serially.

recall.question: What happens during divergence in a warp?
recall.answer: During divergence, lanes of a warp take different branches. The warp then executes both paths serially.

keyTerms.definition: One thread per warp: no divergence possible, but no lockstep amortization either.
Vanish without a full warp.

recall.question: Warp size were 1. What breaks and what gets simpler?
recall.answer: Warp 1: no divergence possible (each thread independent), but no lockstep amortization either, shuffle/vote intrinsics vanish and scheduling overhead per thread rises.

keyTerms.definition: Costs about 2x the uniform branch at warp granularity.
The unit at which divergence costs.

recall.question: State the divergence-cost hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: the divergent branch costs ~2x the uniform branch at warp granularity. Report both timings.

keyTerms.definition: The 32 threads of a warp touch adjacent addresses, merging into minimal transactions.
Minimal memory transactions.

recall.question: Define coalesced access in one line.
recall.answer: Coalesced: the 32 threads of a warp touch adjacent addresses, merging into minimal transactions.

keyTerms.definition: An access pattern where addresses sit 2 bytes apart multiplied by 8 to give 16-byte spacing.
A 2-byte data format used here to compute stride spacing and total memory coverage per warp.

recall.question: How many memory transactions occur when 32 threads with stride 8 access fp16 data?
recall.answer: Four transactions occur because the 32 threads span 512 bytes, which equals four cache lines.

keyTerms.definition: Each thread pulls its own cache line.
Fix: fix index math or stage through shared memory.

recall.question: Each thread pulls its own cache line. Name the access pattern.
recall.answer: Strided or scattered access: each thread pulls its own cache line. Fix the index math or stage via shared.

keyTerms.definition: fp32 stride 1: 128 bytes = 4 transactions, no longer 1.
Grow as lines shrink.

recall.question: Lines were 32 bytes. Stride 1 fp32 transactions?
recall.answer: 32-byte lines, fp32 stride 1: 32*4 = 128 bytes = 4 transactions (no longer 1).

keyTerms.definition: Steps up with each new cache line touched, ~32x at stride 32.
The worst case here.

recall.question: State the stride-curve hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: copy time steps up with each new cache line touched, ~32x at stride 32. Report the curve.

keyTerms.definition: Splits the working set into blocks sized for on-chip memory.
Tiling reuses each loaded element many times.

recall.question: Define tiling in one line.
recall.answer: Tiling splits the working set into blocks sized for on-chip memory, reusing each loaded element many times.

keyTerms.definition: Each A element read 1024 times, once per k.
16 reads: 64x fewer A reads.

recall.question: (1024,1024,1024), tile 64. A HBM reads vs naive.
recall.answer: Naive: each A element read 1024 times (once per k). Tiled (64): 1024/64 = 16 times. 64x fewer A reads.

keyTerms.definition: Or registers: the tile does not fit the per-block budget.
The on-chip limit.

recall.question: Tiled kernel fails to launch. Name the resource.
recall.answer: Shared memory (or registers): the tile does not fit the per-block budget.

keyTerms.definition: Using one tile for the whole matrix means each element loads only once.
The limit for this approach becomes registers per thread.

recall.question: What is the limit when using one tile for the whole matrix?
recall.answer: The limit becomes registers per thread.

keyTerms.definition: Time falls with tile size until shared memory caps it, then launch fails.
Report it.

recall.question: State the tile-size hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: time falls with tile size until shared memory caps it, then launch fails. Report the best tile.

keyTerms.definition: Barrier: all threads in the block reach it before any proceeds.
Writes before it are visible after it.

recall.question: What does __syncthreads guarantee?
recall.answer: __syncthreads guarantees all threads in the block reach the barrier before any proceeds: writes before the barrier are visible after it.

keyTerms.definition: 1e6 * 20 cycles.
The time unit.

recall.question: With 1e6 barriers at 20 cycles each, what is the total cycle count?
recall.answer: 1e6 * 20 = 2e7 cycles.

keyTerms.definition: Threads not taking the if never reach __syncthreads: deadlock.
The block hangs.

recall.question: Kernel hangs. A barrier sits inside an if. Explain.
recall.answer: Divergent barrier: threads not taking the if never reach __syncthreads, so the block deadlocks.

keyTerms.definition: Execution units that cannot share data directly without shared memory.
A memory mechanism that blocks require to share data with each other.

recall.question: How can blocks share data with each other?
recall.answer: Blocks can share data only via global memory with kernel-boundary synchronization through separate launches.

keyTerms.definition: Causes wrong answers first at loads feeding shared reads.
Report which one breaks the sum.

recall.question: State the barrier-removal hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: removing barriers causes wrong answers first at loads feeding shared reads. Report which barrier breaks the sum.

keyTerms.definition: Active warps divided by max warps per SM.
The numerator.

recall.question: Define occupancy.
recall.answer: Occupancy = active warps / max warps per SM.

keyTerms.definition: 8 blocks by shared and by threads: 8*8/64.

recall.question: Toy above. Occupancy at 12 KB/ block?
recall.answer: 12 KB/block: by_shared = 100//12 = 8 blocks, by_threads = 2048//256 = 8, 8*8/64 = 100%.

keyTerms.definition: Bandwidth, not warps, is the limit.
Divergence or bank conflicts.

recall.question: The kernel is slow but not occupancy-bound. Name two other suspects.
recall.answer: Suspects: memory-bound kernel (bandwidth, not warps), or instruction stalls (divergence, bank conflicts).

keyTerms.definition: The section reports that register pressure vanishes in E24.
The section states that threads per SM remain in E24.

recall.question: What vanishes in E24 according to the section?
recall.answer: Register pressure vanishes in E24. Threads per SM and shared memory per block remain.

keyTerms.definition: Time improves with occupancy to ~50% then flattens.

recall.question: State the knee hypothesis.
recall.answer: Hypothesis: time improves with occupancy to ~50% then flattens. Report the knee.

Memory bandwidth that saturates according to the E35 hypothesis and reaches its maximum capacity.
